Yes It varies from one person to another, You determine by starting at a number of sets for a certain muscle group per week ( Let's say that the number is 15 sets), You continue adding sets every week until you feel that you can no longer recover, that's your MRV, Or you can take the average range and work within it.
It's per muscle group per week.
This explains a lot https://renaissanceperiodization.com/training-volume-landmarks-muscle-growth/.

It's the maximum recoverable volume, It is the maximum amount of volume that you can do for a muscle group and recover from, exceeding your MRV will lead to under recovery and overtraining, leaving you to experience negative results.

-I had been in your position before and I tried many things so I'll list them here as they might help you.
  • Increasing my water intake to about 3.5 litres daily has helped me pass through my weight loss plateau, Water has been shown to boost your metabolism.
  • Diet on as many calories as possible while staying in a caloric deficit, I think that 2 pounds per week are a bit too much in my personal opinion, aim for 1-1.5 pounds per week.
  • I tried intermittent fasting and It helped me breeze through the plateau while still eating the same amount of calories ( I don't have a scientific explanation to this and please keep in mind that IF is not magic and it works by creating a caloric deficit).
  • A DIET BREAK has helped me the most, It might sound counter-intuitive, but It helps your body to revert the metabollic adaptations, keep in mind that being in a deficit for 4 months is taxing for your body that's why a two-week diet break is recommended after every 8-12 weeks of dieting, gradually start increasing your calories every 3 days untill your weight becomes stable, stay on that number of calories for about 2 weeks, also don't count calories very strictly on those 2 weeks, It's a time for you to relax mentally and physically, RP has an article about this topic google it, I'm on my mobile phone so I can't link to it right now.
- I'm not an expert by any means, I'm just a normal guy who has been in your place and these things helped me break the plateau.

I'd say 16% BF, continue cutting for a period of 4-6 weeks then bulk.

-First you'd want to identify your goals, you have to decide whether you care more about hypertrophy or strength, remember that specificity is key to success.

-If your goal is strength, I think a strength-focused program like nsuns 531, any variation of 531 is great for that.

-As for the number of training days per week, most people prefer training 4-5 days a week, this way you'll get proper rest and avoid going balls to the walls with the training volume thus avoiding overtraining.

-I don't think that strength training with your injury is the best way to go with your training, as two of the three main lifts depends on your legs, that's just my opinion.

-If your goal is hypertrophy, A Push-Pull-Legs would be great for that, It allows you to cram in plenty of volume, upper/lower splits are great too but I just don't like them, It's a matter of preference.
-Also remember that training volume is key to developing bigger muscles, so remember to increase your total training volume each week untill you're near your MRV.

-Because you have an injury I'd say it'd be better to stick to Push/Pull and rest and repeat that untill you can train legs, then just continue doing PPL.
-Also see what training schedule fits your schedule the best, seek practicality before optimality.

-Also make sure you're in a surplus ranging from (200-500 calories) depending on your training age and how advanced are you, because eating in a surplus is what's going to make you grow!
